name: Crisis Text Line
description: Crisis Text Line provides free 24/7 crisis support via text message, connecting people in crisis with trained counselors.
one_liner: Text HOME to 741741 to reach a trained volunteer crisis counselor by text, 24/7 and free, in the US.
best_for: People in crisis who would rather text than talk on the phone
Teens and young adults who feel more comfortable texting
Anyone who can't speak out loud safely or privately right now
not_for: Life-threatening emergencies or immediate danger: call 911
Ongoing therapy or a regular counselor
People who want a licensed clinician (counselors are trained volunteers)
short_description: A free 24/7 text line: text HOME to 741741 and a trained volunteer crisis counselor texts back.
long_description: Crisis Text Line is a nonprofit text-based crisis service. In the US you text HOME to 741741 and are connected with a trained volunteer crisis counselor, supported by staff, who helps you calm down, think through next steps and stay safe. It is meant for a single crisis conversation, not ongoing care. In January 2022 it ended a data-sharing arrangement with its for-profit spin-off Loris.ai after public criticism; it says conversation data is de-identified before research use and that you can text DELETE to have your identifiable data removed. Published evaluations are post-conversation surveys of texters, not randomized trials.

sections.title: About Crisis Text Line
sections.text: Crisis Text Line is a free, 24/7 text-based mental health support service that connects people in crisis with trained crisis counselors. Founded in 2013, Crisis Text Line has become one of the largest crisis intervention services in the United States, processing millions of text conversations with people experiencing emotional distress, anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts, relationship issues, and other challenges. The text-based format makes support accessible to those who prefer written communication over phone calls.

sections.title: How to Use Crisis Text Line
sections.text: Text HOME to 741741 from anywhere in the United States. You can also text from Canada (text HOME to 686868), UK (text HELLO to 85258), or Ireland (text HELLO to 50808). When you text, you'll receive an automated response while being connected to a live, trained crisis counselor. The counselor will introduce themselves and ask how they can help. Conversations typically last 15-45 minutes and are completely confidential.

sections.title: Trained Crisis Counselors
sections.text: Crisis Text Line counselors are trained volunteers who complete a rigorous 30-hour training program and ongoing education. They are supervised by licensed clinical professionals during every shift. Counselors use collaborative problem-solving and active listening techniques to help texters move from a hot moment to a cool calm. The service uses data and technology to improve crisis intervention while maintaining strict privacy standards.

sections.title: Privacy and Safety
sections.text: Crisis Text Line takes privacy seriously. Conversations are encrypted and confidential. The organization maintains strict data protection policies and does not share personal information without consent. In rare cases where there is immediate danger to life, Crisis Text Line may contact emergency services—but this happens in less than 1% of conversations. The service is designed to be discreet, making it easier for people in sensitive situations to reach out.

privacy.notes: Says it has never monetized identifiable data and lets you text DELETE; ended Loris.ai data sharing in 2022; whether its website shares data with ad partners could not be confirmed.

faqs.q: How do I reach Crisis Text Line?
faqs.a: Text HOME to 741741 from anywhere in the US to connect with a trained crisis counselor. Conversations are free, confidential, and available 24/7.

Trained volunteer crisis counselors answer texts. They complete 30+ hours of training in crisis intervention and are supervised by mental health professionals. They're there to listen and help you through difficult moments.
Yes, conversations are confidential and you don't need to share identifying information. The only exception is if there's imminent risk to life, where counselors follow safety protocols.

faqs.q: What qualifies as a crisis for Crisis Text Line?
faqs.a: Any overwhelming emotional distress—anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts, relationship issues, abuse, grief. You don't need to be suicidal to reach out. If you're struggling emotionally, Crisis Text Line is there.

citation.title: Crisis text-line interventions: Evaluation of texters' perceptions of effectiveness

clinical_trials.outcome: Nearly 90% of suicidal texters said the conversation helped; only 22.5% of texters completed the survey and there was no longer follow-up.

primary_uses: Getting through an emotional crisis by text
Talking through thoughts of suicide or self-harm
Calming down after panic, conflict or overwhelming stress
Being pointed to local services and next steps

patient_summary: If you're struggling and would rather text than call, you can text HOME to 741741 at any time. A trained volunteer crisis counselor will text with you to help you get through the moment and plan what to do next. It's free, and you can text DELETE afterwards to ask for your data to be removed.
